claims.statement: From 11 September 2026, CRA manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents affecting products with digital elements.
The CRA reporting sequence includes an early warning within 24 hours, a full notification within 72 hours, and later final reports with event-dependent deadlines.
The CRA Single Reporting Platform is scheduled to be operational for the reporting start date, while the CRA's main product obligations apply from 11 December 2027.

contrary_evidence: The EU Single Reporting Platform is the free authoritative submission channel, so a relay cannot rely on exclusive access.
Micro and small enterprises have some penalty relief for failures to meet the 24-hour deadline, which may reduce urgency in the initial target segment.

economics.acquisition_route: Run tabletop drills for five OEMs sourced by one conformity lab or embedded-software partner, convert to retainers, then distribute a co-branded readiness package
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 500 manufacturers at 24000 PLN recurring revenue yields 12m PLN ARR; at 20% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 70% founder ownership, equity could exceed 6.7m PLN in years 6-8. Incident fees are upside, not required in the base path, and retained cash is not double-counted.
economics.founder_time: 3 hours per day for product and partner work; a contracted security incident responder must cover on-call cases before launch
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 65-80% because automation handles intake and timelines but security judgement and on-call coverage remain human-intensive
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 10-16 months at 12 retainers averaging 22000 PLN, subject to substantial validation of on-call cost and insurance
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 12000-36000 PLN annual retainer per manufacturer including drills and product inventory, plus 4000-15000 PLN per activated incident
economics.retention_or_repeat: Readiness must persist, products and components change, disclosure intake must stay live, and historical drills/incidents create switching cost even when incidents are rare

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned software-component-to-product map plus precedent timelines and correction outcomes makes triage faster and enables defensible portfolio-wide notification
fingerprint.customer: EU small and mid-sized manufacturers of IoT devices, industrial controllers, connected wellness devices, and packaged software with no 24/7 product security team
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label through conformity labs, firmware engineering firms, insurers, and penetration-test providers; supplier component matches generate portfolio-wide alerts
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Vulnerability intake, component/product resolution, timed approval workflow, evidence vault, and Single Reporting Platform submission support
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer pays an annual readiness retainer and a capped incident activation fee when a reportable case is opened
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The manufacturer learns of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident and the CRA reporting clock starts

founder_fit: Strong data and automation fit, especially component matching and timed workflow design
No personal brand or camera presence is required
Can validate with tabletop drills while keeping the corporate job
Requires delegated security expertise, which keeps the founder away from non-delegable on-call overload
risks: A missed deadline or incorrect non-report decision has severe liability and reputational consequences.
True 24/7 response may be incompatible with a solo founder until coverage is contracted.
Cybersecurity consultancies and product-security platforms can enter the niche.

structure.control_point: the statutory 24-hour and 72-hour reporting clock after awareness of a covered vulnerability or incident
structure.critical_dependency: trusted 24/7 intake and correct determination of product scope, severity, exploitation, and reporting responsibility

thesis: Create an always-on but highly automated reporting relay for small European manufacturers of connected products that lack a full product-security incident response team. It receives vulnerability reports at the manufacturer's disclosure address, resolves the affected product and component, starts the statutory clock, gathers a minimum evidence packet, routes accountable approvals, and submits a coherent 24-hour warning, 72-hour notification, and final report through the Cyber Resilience Act Single Reporting Platform. Enter through CE/conformity labs, embedded-software firms, product-liability insurers, and security testers that already touch many OEMs. The durable moat is a cross-product component dependency graph and incident-timeline corpus that improves triage, while pricing as a retainer plus incident fee aligns revenue with readiness rather than fear-based consulting.
title: CRA 24/72 Incident Evidence Relay
uncertainties: Reportable-event frequency and therefore perceived value of a retainer
Whether insurers and conformity labs will distribute rather than build or refer to established security firms
Minimum security certifications, staffing, and liability cover buyers will demand
